item.title: The Last Dry Seat

turns.text: Make a silent 15-second widescreen short in three scenes. A young woman with a curly black bob and yellow raincoat finds a wet park bench. An older man with a white beard and blue coat offers his folded newspaper to sit on. They sit together and smile. Live-action look, sweet rather than cheesy.

item.tests: Turns two described characters and a simple story into one assembled 15-second film with a readable setup, kind gesture and resolution.

answer_sheet.Characters: A young adult woman with a curly black bob and yellow raincoat; an older adult man with a white beard and blue coat.
answer_sheet.Story and setting: A wet park bench; the woman finds it wet, the man offers his folded newspaper as a dry seat, then they sit together and smile.
answer_sheet.Length and format: One 15-second widescreen 16:9 video, with three scenes.
answer_sheet.Sound, dialogue and text: Silent, with no dialogue, captions or titles.

must_haves: One playable 15-second widescreen film contains three sequential scenes, not separate clip deliverables.
The woman has a curly black bob and yellow raincoat; the man has a white beard and blue coat.
The opening visibly establishes that the park bench is wet.
The man offers a folded newspaper as a dry place to sit, and the ending shows both characters seated together and smiling.
The film has a live-action appearance and no audible soundtrack.

I'm on the free plan and don't want my credits burned, so tell me what this will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t started any generation or spent generation credits.** I can plan the short, but this connection doesn’t expose your credit balance or a live video-cost estimate, so I can’t honestly quote an exact price before running it.

### Proposed short
Silent, **15 seconds, 16:9 widescreen**, live-action look:
- **0–5s:** A young adult woman with a curly black bob and yellow raincoat approaches a rain-soaked park bench and pauses.
- **5–10s:** An older man with a white beard and blue coat notices, then quietly offers his folded newspaper to cover the wet seat.
- **10–15s:** They sit together, exchange a small smile, and look out across the park. Natural performances—no exaggerated reaction or sentimental effects.

### Lower-cost options
| Option | Trade-off |
|---|---|
| **15 seconds at 480p, using a free-plan video model** | Preserves the full story. I can request all three scenes in one generation, though precise cuts and character continuity aren’t guaranteed. |
| **8–10 seconds at 480p** | Likely cheaper if billed by duration; compresses the action and leaves less time for the ending. Exact savings are unverified. |
| **5-second test at 480p** | Smaller initial commitment: test just the newspaper offer and restrained smiles before funding a longer version. |
| **Three-panel still storyboard at 640px** | A lower-cost way to review the story visually, but not a moving short. A free-plan Flux model starts at **5 credits for one image**; a single image could contain all three panels. |

**My recommendation:** verify the price for one silent 15-second, 480p generation before committing; use a 5-second test if that quote is too high. 480p is the lowest video resolution exposed here, and I wouldn’t add reference-image generation or separate scene jobs without your approval.

If you can share the estimate shown in Magic Hour, I can help compare it with the shorter options. **I’ll hold off on all generation until you approve a verified cost.**

Do you mean the **full 15-second short** or the **5-second test**?

I still can’t verify the credit cost through this connection. Since you asked to approve the cost first, I haven’t started anything. Please share Magic Hour’s estimate for your choice so we can confirm it before spending credits.
dialog.user: The 5-second test—ok, go ahead with that.

turns.agent:
The 5-second test was **refused because your account has insufficient credits**. No video was generated, and I haven’t retried.

I can’t see your balance or the exact credit shortfall, so I can’t confirm whether a shorter clip would fit. We can keep the storyboard as a no-cost plan, or you can share your balance and Magic Hour’s estimate before another attempt.

approvals.name: create_video_from_text

style.prompt: Silent live-action short, 5 seconds, widescreen. One continuous naturalistic medium-wide two-shot in a quiet park just after light rain, soft overcast daylight, realistic skin and wet surfaces, understated independent-film cinematography. A young adult woman with a curly black bob wearing a yellow raincoat stands beside a visibly wet wooden park bench. An older adult man with a white beard wearing a blue coat sits at one end. He notices her hesitation, gently offers his folded newspaper and lays it flat on the empty wet seat beside him. She sits on the newspaper next to him and they exchange a small, genuine smile. Keep the offer clear and the action simple and plausible. Sweet, restrained human kindness rather than cheesy romance; subtle acting, no exaggerated gestures. Stable camera, consistent faces and clothing. No dialogue, no music, no sound, no captions, no titles.
